title: clarify-decision-responsibilities-and-timing-for-prd-slice-acceptance
creator: Anika Bose
description: Objective: Define a timeboxed, role-specific acceptance pathway for a scoped PRD slice (model onboarding + telemetry), reduce last-minute scope churn at handoff, and create a lightweight sign-off checklist that legal, design, and engineering can execute within 48 hours of review. Background: Recent onboarding slices have stalled when legal requested additional dataflow diagrams after design had shipped mocks and engineering had started infra work. This ticket aligns owners, timelines, and minimal artifacts required for a valid sign-off to reduce rework and speed up release gating. Success is measured by reducing review cycles for PRD slices from an average of 7 days to <= 3 days and preventing infra rework caused by late-scope changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each sign-off lane (Design, Eng, Legal) has a single named owner and a 48-hour SLA for initial review after artifacts are posted.
- PRD slice checklist is attached to the PRD and contains required artifacts for each lane (design comps + interaction notes, engineering runbook + infra assumptions, legal dataflow + retention notes).
- No infra work marked as "started" in engineering without an approved engineering runbook and a legal minimal-acceptance flag.
- All dependencies (ENG-11234, DES-991, LEGAL-210) resolved or assigned with explicit mitigation steps before release cutoff.
- A retrospective note is auto-created after sign-off capturing any outstanding concerns and next actions.
decisions: Adopt 48-hour SLA for initial review; escalate to PM if no response in SLA window.
Use a slim dataflow skeleton for legal to sign off on (high level diagram + PII/residency table) instead of full architecture docs for initial acceptance.
Engineering will tag infra work as 'blocked-by-legal' when legal acceptance is outstanding to prevent wasted implementation effort.
Design to publish a single canonical comps folder and include an 'interaction notes' file enumerating edge cases for legal/engineering reviewers.
PMs owning slices are responsible for triage and escalation; PM will host weekly 30-minute alignment calls while this process phases in.
